40 1. Introduction 41 Among  the  biomass  utilization  technologies,  chemical  looping  gasification 42 (CLG) stands out as the one with the lowest energy and economic cost in converting 43 biomass  into  syngas  (H2,  CO)  or  H2  rich  gas[1-3].  The  conventional  gasification 44 agents are replaced by lattice oxygen which is generated from Oxygen carrier (OC). 45 In a typical CLG system, OC is circulated between an air reactor and a fuel reactor. In 46 the fuel reactor, biomass reacts with OC and is converted to H2, CO, CH4 as well as 47 CO2. After contributing the lattice oxygen, OC is reduced to a low valence oxide or 48 simple substances. The reduced OC, together with the unconverted biomass fractions 49 (char),  are  fed  into  the  air  reactor,  to  heat  up  the  OC  and  burn  off  the  char.  The 50 reduced OC is oxidized again into high valence oxide when contacting with oxygen, 51 subsequently,  transmitted  into  the  fuel  reactor  to  provide  the  heat  necessary  for 52 gasification[4-6]. 53 To date, much of the research has focused on finding the appropriate OC for the 54 process since it is one of the keystones in the development of the CLG technology. 55 Low  cost  gives  natural  ores  a  critical  advantage  over  other  candidates.  As  a 56 magnesium-iron-silicate,  olivine,  has  been  extensively  tested  in  the  laboratory  and 57 large-scale experiments owing to its satisfying crushing strength, abrasion resistance 58 and  catalytic  activity[8].  Large-scale  tests  has  been  carried  out  to  evaluate  the 59 performance  of  olivine  in  the  2-4  MWth  indirect  biomass  gasification  unit  using 60 wood chips [9], in which 30% tar destruction was obtained by olivine as bed material. 61 Ryd´en  et  al[10]  assessed  the  crushing  behavior  of  25  materials  by  a  spray  cup, Preprint not peer reviewed

Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) 186 2.3.1 Thermogravimetric multiple redox experiments 187 A 10-cyclic isothermal reduction-oxidation experiments of the prepared OCs were 188 conducted in a TGA (SDT Q600, TA Instruments) at 189 carrying behavior and stability of OCs. Prior to each TGA test, about 30 190 OC, supported on a ceramic crucible, was heated in air atmosphere up to 191 heating rate of 10℃/min. The 10%H2 + 90%N2, providing reduction atmosphere, was 192 passed in the reduction stage with a reduction time of precisely 15 minutes. After the 193 reduction step, the OC was exposed to air for 10 min in the oxidation stage. It is worth 194 noting that the contact of H2 and O2 at the border of the oxidation stage and reduction 195 stage has been avoided by N2 which was introduced as purging gas for 5 min. Mass 196 flow meter controller is used to ensure that the gas is passed through at a flow rate of 197 100 mL/min at each stage. 198 2.3.2 Thermogravimetric analysis coupled to infrared spectroscopy 199 The non-isothermal reaction between OCs and CS were quantitatively 200 determined in a TG-FTIR (TGA 8000, Perkin Elmer), which was capable of real-time 201 weighing  the  changes  of  mass  and  measuring  the  gasification  products.  Mixture  of 202 CS (4 ± 0.2 mg) and OCs (40 ± 0.2 mg) were heated from 40  o C to 900  o C (ramp rate 203 of  30 o C/min),  and  then  kept  isothermal  for  about  10  min.  Prior  to  each  test, the 204 adapter inlet, transfer line and TG-FTIR cell are heated from ambient temperature to 205 270 o C, avoiding the condensation of products. FTIR  spectra were obtained 206 continuously in the range of 4000-500 cm -1  with resolution of 2 cm -1 . Preprint not peer reviewed

247 In this study, a standard vibrating screen has been used to carried out the attrition 248 tests, according to the GB/T10504-2017, China [18]. Prior to the test, crushed powder 249 in  the  OCs is removed by a standard screen (pore size = 0.25 mm). Approximately 250 100  g  of  OC  (size  ranging  from  0.45  to  0.85  mm),  noted  as  m1,  is  placed  on  a 251 vibrating sieve and shaken continuously for 3 hours, weighing at 30 minutes intervals. 252 When the vibration was completed, two standard screens, with pore size of 0.25 mm 253 and 0.15 mm, are used to separate broken particles and abrasive powders, which are 254 noted as m2 and m3, respectively. It could be observed 406 from the DTG profile that two individual reaction zones, occurring in sequence, were 407 detected. The first reaction zone (zone 1), occurring at the temperature from 300 to 408 600 ℃, was  attributed  to  the  emission  of  volatiles  with  fast  weight  loss,  where 409 maximum weight loss 5.90 wt.% was obtained in 900-Cu/Ni/O and 1100-Cu/Ni/O at 410 the  same  time. Conclusions 591 The main goal behind the present investigation was to raise the performances of 592 olivine used into BCLG by adding copper oxides and nickel oxides. The study was 593 focalized  on  optimization  and  characterization  of  OC  in  term  of  the  anti-resistance 594 and reactivity by means of an increase in calcination temperature. The effect of the 595 preparation  temperature  on  the  composition,  morphology,  redox  properties,  oxygen 596 transport capacity, attrition rate and activity of the OCs is clarified. 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 Preprint not peer reviewed

605 1.93% were obtained for 900-Cu/Ni/O, 1100-Cu/Ni/O and 1300-Cu/Ni/O, 606 respectively. Correspondingly, the final weight loss of OCs with CS also showed the 607 same  trend  as  redox  process  of  OCs. The  infrared  absorption  peaks  of  CO2  in  the 608 product are particularly distinct, with the larger the oxygen-carrying capacity the more 609 CO2 is produced by the OC. 610 In  MFBR  tests,  the  amount  of  OC  used  in  the  gasifier  strongly  affects  the 611 performance of the CLG process, leading to upward trend in total gas yield as well as 612 carbon conversion efficiency and a downward trend in lower heating valve, but excess 613 amount of OC will further consume H2 and CO to form H2O and CO2. The increment 614 of  temperature  significantly  enhances  the  gas  yield  and  the  process  efficiency.  The 615 main variable affecting to the process performance parameters was the steam injection 616 ratio, where the content of H2 has been trending upward with the steam amount used, 617 reaching a peak of about 0.35 Nm 3 /kg for the 1100-Cu/Ni/O at steam injection ratio of 618 0.075  g/min.  Additionally,  higher  steam  injection  ratio  also  enhances  the  carbon 619 conversion,  the  gas  yield  and  gasification  efficiency.  However,  excess  steam  may 620 cause a decline in the BCLG performance due to heat loss in the gasifier. Interestingly 621 to  note  that  the  calcination  temperature  strongly  influences  the  reactivity  of  OCs  in 622 the  BCLG.  Under  optimal  operating  conditions,  1100-Cu/Ni/O  gives  averagely  a 623 better  result  in  terms  of  CO  production  with  a  greater  gas  yield  of  0.31  Nm 3 /kg  as 624 well as higher gasification efficiencies of 59.2%, while the carbon conversion of the 625 1100-Cu/Ni/O is lower than that of 900-Cu/Ni/O with about 7%. A  stable 626 performance was also observed during a 10-cyle test with 1100-Cu/Ni/O, suggesting Preprint not peer reviewed
